text:
Leah: Anyone else hitting repeated login prompts when their ~/.redwood is a symlink into a git repo? redwoodctl 0.25.0 (homebrew) on macOS 13.6 keeps asking to auth every new shell.
Tony: That's odd. What's the symlink target and do you see a token file?
Leah: ~/.redwood -> ~/dotfiles/redwood
Leah: After `redwoodctl auth login` I see a temp file in /var/folders/... like `redwood-token.tmp` but no token in the target dir.
Arjun: Sounds like atomic-write+rename is failing across different filesystems/inodes. On macOS the temp dir may be on a different volume for sandboxed/homebrew-installed binaries.
Leah: `redwoodctl auth whoami` right after login returns my user, but immediately the next CLI call 401s and asks to login again.
Tony: Workaround: set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=$HOME/dotfiles/redwood` and login; CLI writes directly and the loop stops.
Leah: Confirmed, that fixes it. But this is annoying for dotfiles users.
Arjun: Filing DEVEX-5178. Plan: attempt os.Rename; on EXDEV fallback to write to resolved target or copy+chmod. Add unit/integration test that creates a symlinked config dir and simulates cross-device rename.
ci-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-5178 assigned to @arjun, priority P1.
Leah: Can we also add a short note in the CLI troubleshooting doc with the env workaround? I can draft the blurb.
Tony: We'll add a homebrew/darwin e2e in CI that runs the bottled binary with a symlinked config dir.
Arjun: I'll open a small patch and ping @leah for validation when a beta is ready.
Leah: happy to smoke test :rocket: 
devex-bot: Labeling DEVEX-5178: `auth`, `symlink`, `darwin`.
